sanskrit: yaḥ śastrabhṛc chreṣṭhatamaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; pitāmahaṃ vyākṣipad alpacetāḥ saṃkhyāyamāno 'rdharathaḥ sa kaccit; tvayā hato 'dyādhirathir durātmā
english: That dull-witted wretch who, though reckoned but half a chariot-warrior, dared to revile the foremost weapon-bearer on earth, our grandsire — that vile son of Adhiratha — has he been slain by you this day?

sanskrit: amarṣaṇaṃ nikṛtisamīraṇeritaṃ; hṛdi śritaṃ jvalanam imaṃ sadā mama hato mayā so 'dya sametya pāpadhīr; iti bruvan praśamaya me 'dya phalguna
english: This unrelenting fire, fanned ever by his treachery, lodged within my heart — quench it for me today, O Phalguna, by saying: "That evil-minded man I met and slew this day."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tad dharmaśīlasya vaco niśamya; rājñaḥ kruddhasyādhirathau mahātmā uvāca durdharṣam adīnasattvaṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ jiṣṇur anantavīryaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard those words of the righteous king, enraged at the son of Adhiratha, the great-souled and victorious Arjuna, of boundless might, spoke thus to the indomitable, undaunted Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: saṃśaptakair yudhyamānasya me 'dya; senāgrayāyī kurusainyasya rājan āśīviṣābhān khagamān pramuñcan; drauṇiḥ purastāt sahasā vyatiṣṭhat
english: As I was fighting today with the Saṃśaptakas, O king, the son of Droṇa, the vanguard of the Kuru host, suddenly took his stand before me, loosing arrows that flew like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ meghanibhaṃ mamemam; ambaṣṭhasenā maraṇe vyatiṣṭhat teṣām ahaṃ pañca śatāni hatvā; tato drauṇim agamaṃ pārthivāgrya
english: Seeing this cloud-like chariot of mine, the Ambaṣṭha host stood firm, ready to die. Having slain five hundred of them, I then came upon the son of Droṇa, O foremost of kings.

sanskrit: tato 'parān bāṇasaṃghān anekān; ākarṇapūrṇāyatavipramuktān sasarja śikṣāstrabalaprayatnais; tathā yathā prāvṛṣi kālameghaḥ
english: Then he discharged volley upon volley of arrows, drawn to the ear and loosed at full stretch, by the force of his training and the strength of his weapons — even as the rain-cloud pours down in the season of storms.

sanskrit: naivādadānaṃ na ca saṃdadhānaṃ; jānīmahe katareṇāsyatīti vāmena vā yadi vā dakṣiṇena; sa droṇaputraḥ samare paryavartat
english: We could not tell when he took an arrow nor when he fitted it, nor by which hand — the left or the right — he would let it fly: so swiftly did that son of Droṇa wheel about in the battle.

sanskrit: avidhyan māṃ pañcabhir droṇaputraḥ; śitaiḥ śaraiḥ pañcabhir vāsudevam ahaṃ tu taṃ triṃśatā vajrakalpaiḥ; samārdayaṃ nimiṣasyāntareṇa
english: The son of Droṇa pierced me with five sharp arrows and Vāsudeva with five more; but I, in the space of an eyeblink, crushed him with thirty shafts like thunderbolts.

sanskrit: sa vikṣaran rudhiraṃ sarvagātrai; rathānīkaṃ sūtasūnor viveśa mayābhibhūtaḥ sainikānāṃ prabarhān; asāv apaśyan rudhireṇa pradigdhān
english: Streaming blood from all his limbs, overwhelmed by me, he withdrew into the chariot-ranks of the Sūta's son, not heeding the foremost of his own warriors, all of them drenched in gore.

sanskrit: tato 'bhibhūtaṃ yudhi vīkṣya sainyaṃ; vidhvastayodhaṃ drutavājināgam pañcāśatā rathamukhyaiḥ sametaḥ; karṇas tvaran mām upāyāt pramāthī
english: Then, seeing his army crushed in the fight, its warriors scattered, its horses and elephants in flight, the destroyer Karṇa, joined by fifty chief chariot-warriors, came swiftly against me.

sanskrit: tān sūdayitvāham apāsya karṇaṃ; draṣṭuṃ bhavantaṃ tvarayābhiyātaḥ sarve pāñcālā hy udvijante sma karṇād; gandhād gāvaḥ kesariṇo yathaiva
english: Having destroyed them and left Karṇa aside, I hastened to see you; for all the Pāñcālas shrink from Karṇa as cattle shrink from the scent of a lion.

sanskrit: mahājhaṣasyeva mukhaṃ prapannāḥ; prabhadrakāḥ karṇam abhi dravanti mṛtyor āsyaṃ vyāttam ivānvapadyan; prabhadrakāḥ karṇam āsādya rājan
english: Like men plunging into the mouth of a great fish, the Prabhadrakas rush upon Karṇa; encountering Karṇa, O king, the Prabhadrakas enter as into the gaping jaws of Death.

sanskrit: āyāhi paśyādya yuyutsamānaṃ; māṃ sūtaputraṃ ca vṛtau jayāya ṣaṭsāhasrā bhārata rājaputrāḥ; svargāya lokāya rathā nimagnāḥ
english: Come and behold today both me and the Sūta's son, each resolved on victory and eager for the fray. Six thousand royal princes, O Bhārata, those chariot-warriors, have sunk down — bound for heaven and its world.

sanskrit: sametyāhaṃ sūtaputreṇa saṃkhye; vṛtreṇa vajrīva narendramukhya yotsye bhṛśaṃ bhārata sūtaputram; asmin saṃgrāme yadi vai dṛśyate 'dya
english: Meeting the Sūta's son in battle, O foremost of kings, as the Thunderer met Vṛtra, I shall fight him hard, O Bhārata — that son of the Sūta — if only he shows himself in this engagement today.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ na ced adya nihanmi rājan; sabāndhavaṃ yudhyamānaṃ prasahya pratiśrutyākurvatāṃ vai gatir yā; kaṣṭāṃ gaccheyaṃ tām ahaṃ rājasiṃha
english: If today I do not by main force slay Karṇa as he fights, together with his kinsmen, O king, then may I go to that grievous fate that awaits those who promise and do not perform, O lion among kings.

sanskrit: āmantraye tvāṃ brūhi jayaṃ raṇe me; purā bhīmaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrā grasante sautiṃ haniṣyāmi narendrasiṃha; sainyaṃ tathā śatrugaṇāṃś ca sarvān
english: I take my leave of you — wish me victory in battle, before the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra overwhelm Bhīma. I shall slay the Sūta's son, O lion among men, and his army, and all the hosts of our foes.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutvā karṇaṃ kalyam udāravīryaṃ; kruddhaḥ pārthaḥ phalgunasyāmitaujāḥ dhanaṃjayaṃ vākyam uvāca cedaṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ karṇaśarābhitaptaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing that Karṇa was hale and of lofty valor, the king Yudhiṣṭhira, tormented by Karṇa's arrows, grew wrathful and spoke these words to Phalguna, to Dhanaṃjaya of measureless might:

sanskrit: idaṃ yadi dvaitavane hy avakṣyaḥ; karṇaṃ yoddhuṃ na prasahe nṛpeti vayaṃ tadā prāptakālāni sarve; vṛttāny upaiṣyāma tadaiva pārtha
english: Had you said this back in the Dvaita forest — "O king, I cannot bring myself to fight Karṇa" — then, O Pārtha, we would all have taken such measures as the hour demanded, then and there.

sanskrit: mayi pratiśrutya vadhaṃ hi tasya; balasya cāptasya tathaiva vīra ānīya naḥ śatrumadhyaṃ sa kasmāt; samutkṣipya sthaṇḍile pratyapiṃṣṭhāḥ
english: Having promised me his death, O hero, and the trusty army with him, why then, having led us into the very midst of the foe, did you lift us up only to dash us down upon the bare ground?

sanskrit: anvāśiṣma vayam arjuna tvayi; yiyāsavo bahu kalyāṇam iṣṭam tan naḥ sarvaṃ viphalaṃ rājaputra; phalārthināṃ nicula ivātipuṣpaḥ
english: We placed our hopes in you, O Arjuna, longing to attain much that is good and desired; yet all that has come to nothing for us, O prince — like the over-flowering nicula tree to those who craved its fruit.

sanskrit: pracchāditaṃ baḍiśam ivāmiṣeṇa; pracchādito gavaya ivāpavācā anarthakaṃ me darśitavān asi tvaṃ; rājyārthino rājyarūpaṃ vināśam
english: Like a hook hidden by its bait, like a wild ox lured by a false call, you have shown me ruin in the guise of a kingdom — to me who sought a kingdom — and to no purpose at all.

sanskrit: yat tat pṛthāṃ vāg uvācāntarikṣe; saptāhajāte tvayi mandabuddhau jātaḥ putro vāsavavikramo 'yaṃ; sarvāñ śūrāñ śātravāñ jeṣyatīti
english: When you, dull-witted one, were but seven days old, a voice from the sky said to Pṛthā: "This son who is born has the prowess of Vāsava; he shall vanquish all the heroes who are your foes."

sanskrit: ayaṃ jetā khāṇḍave devasaṃghān; sarvāṇi bhūtāny api cottamaujāḥ ayaṃ jetā madrakaliṅgakekayān; ayaṃ kurūn hanti ca rājamadhye
english: "This one, of surpassing might, shall conquer at Khāṇḍava the hosts of the gods and all beings besides; this one shall vanquish the Madrakas, the Kaliṅgas, and the Kekayas; this one shall slay the Kurus in the midst of kings."

sanskrit: asmāt paro na bhavitā dhanurdharo; na vai bhūtaḥ kaś cana jātu jetā icchann āryaḥ sarvabhūtāni kuryād; vaśe vaśī sarvasamāptavidyaḥ
english: "No bowman shall ever surpass this one, nor has any ever been who could conquer him. This noble one, master of himself and perfect in every art, could, if he wished, bring all beings under his sway."

sanskrit: kāntyā śaśāṅkasya javena vāyoḥ; sthairyeṇa meroḥ kṣamayā pṛthivyāḥ sūryasya bhāsā dhanadasya lakṣmyā; śauryeṇa śakrasya balena viṣṇoḥ
english: "In beauty he is the equal of the moon, in swiftness of the wind, in steadfastness of Meru, in forbearance of the earth, in radiance of Sūrya, in splendor of the Lord of Wealth, in heroism of Śakra, in strength of Viṣṇu —

sanskrit: tulyo mahātmā tava kunti putro; jāto 'diter viṣṇur ivārihantā sveṣāṃ jayāya dviṣatāṃ vadhāya; khyāto 'mitaujāḥ kulatantukartā
english: so is this great-souled son of yours, O Kuntī — a slayer of foes born as Viṣṇu was born of Aditi: renowned, of measureless might, the preserver of his line, for the victory of his own and the destruction of his enemies."

sanskrit: ity antarikṣe śataśṛṅgamūrdhni; tapasvināṃ śṛṇvatāṃ vāg uvāca evaṃvidhaṃ tvāṃ tac ca nābhūt tavādya; devā hi nūnam anṛtaṃ vadanti
english: Thus spoke the voice from the sky upon the summit of Śataśṛṅga, in the hearing of the ascetics. Yet you have proved to be no such man this day — surely, then, even the gods speak falsehood.

sanskrit: tathāpareṣām ṛṣisattamānāṃ; śrutvā giraṃ pūjayatāṃ sadaiva na saṃnatiṃ praimi suyodhanasya; na tvā jānāmy ādhirather bhayārtam
english: Hearing the like from those other most excellent sages whom we ever revered, I had never thought to bow to Suyodhana — nor did I know you to be one stricken with fear of the son of Adhiratha.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭrā kṛtaṃ vāham akūjanākṣaṃ; śubhaṃ samāsthāya kapidhvajaṃ tvam khaḍgaṃ gṛhītvā hemacitraṃ samiddhaṃ; dhanuś cedaṃ gāṇḍivaṃ tālamātram sa keśavenohyamānaḥ kathaṃ nu; karṇād bhīto vyapayāto 'si pārtha
english: Mounted upon that fair, ape-bannered car wrought by Tvaṣṭṛ, its axles never creaking, grasping your sword bright with gold and this Gāṇḍiva bow as tall as a palm-tree, and borne onward by Keśava himself — how, O Pārtha, could you have turned and fled in fear of Karṇa?

sanskrit: dhanuś caitat keśavāya pradāya; yantābhaviṣyas tvaṃ raṇe ced durātman tato 'haniṣyat keśavaḥ karṇam ugraṃ; marutpatir vṛtram ivāttavajraḥ
english: Had you, base-souled one, handed this bow to Keśava and yourself become the driver in the battle, then Keśava would have slain the fierce Karṇa, as the Lord of the Maruts, thunderbolt in hand, slew Vṛtra.

sanskrit: māse 'patiṣyaḥ pañcame tvaṃ prakṛcchre; na vā garbho 'py abhaviṣyaḥ pṛthāyāḥ tat te śramo rājaputrābhaviṣyan; na saṃgrāmād apayātuṃ durātman
english: Better had you miscarried in the fifth, the perilous, month, or had Pṛthā's womb never borne you at all! That, O prince, would have spared you this toil — better that than to flee from battle, O base-souled one!

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yudhiṣṭhireṇaivam uktaḥ kaunteyaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ asiṃ jagrāha saṃkruddho jighāṃsur bharatarṣabham
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, he of the white steeds, in a great rage seized his sword, bent on slaying the bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tasya kopaṃ samudvīkṣya cittajñaḥ keśavas tadā uvāca kim idaṃ pārtha gṛhītaḥ khaḍga ity uta
english: Seeing his fury, Keśava, the knower of hearts, then said: "What is this, O Pārtha — why have you taken up your sword?"

sanskrit: neha paśyāmi yoddhavyaṃ tava kiṃ cid dhanaṃjaya te dhvastā dhārtarāṣṭrā hi sarve bhīmena dhīmatā
english: "I see no one here for you to fight, O Dhanaṃjaya; for the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra have all been shattered by wise Bhīma."

sanskrit: apayāto 'si kaunteya rājā draṣṭavya ity api sa rājā bhavatā dṛṣṭaḥ kuśalī ca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "You came away from the field, O son of Kuntī, saying the king must be seen; and now you have seen that king, and Yudhiṣṭhira is well."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpaśārdūlaṃ śārdūlasamavikramam harṣakāle tu saṃprāpte kasmāt tvā manyur āviśat
english: "Now that you behold this tiger among kings, of a tiger's own prowess, and the hour for rejoicing has come — why has wrath seized hold of you?"

sanskrit: na taṃ paśyāmi kaunteya yas te vadhyo bhaved iha kasmād bhavān mahākhaḍgaṃ parigṛhṇāti satvaram
english: "I see no one here, O son of Kuntī, who ought to be slain by you. Why then do you so hastily grasp your great sword?"

sanskrit: tat tvā pṛcchāmi kaunteya kim idaṃ te cikīrṣitam parāmṛśasi yat kruddhaḥ khaḍgam adbhutavikrama
english: "This I ask of you, O son of Kuntī, O man of wondrous valor: what is it you mean to do, that in your wrath you lay hold of the sword?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kṛṣṇena prekṣamāṇo yudhiṣṭhiram arjunaḥ prāha govindaṃ kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, his eyes fixed upon Yudhiṣṭhira, spoke to Govinda, hissing in his anger like a serpent:

sanskrit: dada gāṇḍīvam anyasmā iti māṃ yo 'bhicodayet chindyām ahaṃ śiras tasya ity upāṃśuvrataṃ mama
english: "Whoever should urge me, saying 'Give the Gāṇḍiva to another,' him I would behead — such is my secret vow."

sanskrit: tad ukto 'ham adīnātman rājñāmitaparākrama samakṣaṃ tava govinda na tat kṣantum ihotsahe
english: "That very thing has been said to me by the king, O undaunted one of measureless prowess, here before your face, Govinda; and this I cannot bring myself to forgive."

sanskrit: tasmād enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi rājānaṃ dharmabhīrukam pratijñāṃ pālayiṣyāmi hatvemaṃ narasattamam etadarthaṃ mayā khaḍgo gṛhīto yadunandana
english: "Therefore I shall slay this king, scrupulous though he be in dharma; by killing this best of men I shall keep my vow. For this end have I taken up the sword, O delight of the Yadus."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ hatvā satye 'py ānṛṇyatāṃ gataḥ viśoko vijvaraś cāpi bhaviṣyāmi janārdana
english: "So, having slain Yudhiṣṭhira, I shall be discharged of my debt even to truth, and I shall become free of grief and free of fever, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: kiṃ vā tvaṃ manyase prāptam asmin kāle samutthite tvam asya jagatas tāta vettha sarvaṃ gatāgatam tat tathā prakariṣyāmi yathā māṃ vakṣyate bhavān
english: "Or what do you deem fitting in this hour that has now arisen? You, dear one, know all the comings and goings of this world; so shall I act in whatever way you shall direct me."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca idānīṃ pārtha jānāmi na vṛddhāḥ sevitās tvayā akāle puruṣavyāghra saṃrambhakriyayānayā na hi dharmavibhāgajñaḥ kuryād evaṃ dhanaṃjaya
english: Kṛṣṇa said: Now, O Pārtha, I know that you have never attended upon the elders, since at the wrong hour, O tiger among men, you act with such reckless fury. For one who knows the distinctions of dharma would never act thus, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: akāryāṇāṃ ca kāryāṇāṃ saṃyogaṃ yaḥ karoti vai kāryāṇām akriyāṇāṃ ca sa pārtha puruṣādhamaḥ
english: He who treats what ought not to be done as a thing to be done, and what ought to be done as a thing to be left undone — he, O Pārtha, is the basest of men.

sanskrit: anusṛtya tu ye dharmaṃ kavayaḥ samupasthitāḥ samāsavistaravidāṃ na teṣāṃ vettha niścayam
english: You do not know the settled conviction of those seers who, following dharma, have attained it — those who understand it both in brief and at length.

sanskrit: aniścayajño hi naraḥ kāryākāryaviniścaye avaśo muhyate pārtha yathā tvaṃ mūḍha eva tu
english: For a man who lacks sure knowledge in deciding what is to be done and what is not, is helplessly bewildered, O Pārtha — even as you, in your folly, are now bewildered.

sanskrit: na hi kāryam akāryaṃ vā sukhaṃ jñātuṃ kathaṃ cana śrutena jñāyate sarvaṃ tac ca tvaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: It is by no means easy to know what should be done and what should not; all this is known through sacred learning, and that learning you do not comprehend.

sanskrit: avijñānād bhavān yac ca dharmaṃ rakṣati dharmavit prāṇināṃ hi vadhaṃ pārtha dhārmiko nāvabudhyate
english: Out of ignorance you, who deem yourself a knower of dharma, would uphold dharma; but a righteous man, O Pārtha, does not look upon the slaying of living beings as dharma.

sanskrit: prāṇinām avadhas tāta sarvajyāyān mato mama anṛtaṃ tu bhaved vācyaṃ na ca hiṃsyāt kathaṃ cana
english: The non-slaying of living creatures, dear one, I hold to be the highest of all; rather should a falsehood be spoken than that one should ever do harm.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ rājānaṃ dharmakovidam hanyād bhavān naraśreṣṭha prākṛto 'nyaḥ pumān iva
english: How then, O best of men, would you slay your eldest brother, the king, a man learned in dharma — as if you were some other, common man?

sanskrit: ayudhyamānasya vadhas tathāśastrasya bhārata parāṅmukhasya dravataḥ śaraṇaṃ vābhigacchataḥ kṛtāñjaleḥ prapannasya na vadhaḥ pūjyate budhaiḥ
english: The slaying of one who does not fight, who bears no weapon, who turns his back and flees, or who seeks refuge, who joins his palms in supplication or surrenders — such killing, O Bhārata, is not approved by the wise.

sanskrit: tvayā caiva vrataṃ pārtha bālenaiva kṛtaṃ purā tasmād adharmasaṃyuktaṃ mauḍhyāt karma vyavasyasi
english: And this vow of yours, O Pārtha, was made of old when you were but a boy; therefore, out of folly, you now resolve upon a deed bound up with unrighteousness.

sanskrit: sa guruṃ pārtha kasmāt tvaṃ hanyā dharmam anusmaran asaṃpradhārya dharmāṇāṃ gatiṃ sūkṣmāṃ duranvayām
english: How, O Pārtha, would you slay your elder, claiming to be mindful of dharma, without having weighed the course of duties — a course subtle and hard to trace?

sanskrit: idaṃ dharmarahasyaṃ ca vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha yad brūyāt tava bhīṣmo vā dharmajño vā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: And I shall declare to you this secret of dharma, O bull of the Bharatas — what Bhīṣma, or the dharma-knowing Yudhiṣṭhira, might tell you,

sanskrit: viduro vā tathā kṣattā kuntī vāpi yaśasvinī tat te vakṣyāmi tattvena tan nibodha dhanaṃjaya
english: or what Vidura the steward, or even the renowned Kuntī, might say — that I shall tell you in its truth; mark it well, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: satyasya vacanaṃ sādhu na satyād vidyate param tattvenaitat sudurjñeyaṃ yasya satyam anuṣṭhitam
english: To speak the truth is good; there is nothing higher than truth. Yet in its essence this is very hard to know — what truth is, for him who would practice it.

sanskrit: bhavet satyam avaktavyaṃ vaktavyam anṛtaṃ bhavet sarvasvasyāpahāre tu vaktavyam anṛtaṃ bhavet
english: There may be truth that ought not to be told, and falsehood that ought to be told; when one's whole substance is being plundered, a falsehood ought to be spoken.

sanskrit: prāṇātyaye vivāhe ca vaktavyam anṛtaṃ bhavet yatrānṛtaṃ bhavet satyaṃ satyaṃ cāpy anṛtaṃ bhavet
english: When life is at stake, and in matters of marriage, a falsehood ought to be spoken; for there are cases where falsehood becomes truth, and truth itself becomes falsehood.

sanskrit: tādṛśaṃ paśyate bālo yasya satyam anuṣṭhitam satyānṛte viniścitya tato bhavati dharmavit
english: The simple-minded man sees as truth only that truth which he himself has practiced; but only after he has discerned aright between truth and falsehood does one become a knower of dharma.

sanskrit: kim āścaryaṃ kṛtaprajñaḥ puruṣo 'pi sudāruṇaḥ sumahat prāpnuyāt puṇyaṃ balāko 'ndhavadhād iva
english: What wonder is it that even a man of cultivated wisdom, though most cruel, should gain great merit — as Balāka did by slaying the blind one?

sanskrit: kim āścaryaṃ punar mūḍho dharmakāmo 'py apaṇḍitaḥ sumahat prāpnuyāt pāpam āpagām iva kauśikaḥ
english: And what wonder, again, that a fool, devoted to dharma yet unlearned, should incur grievous sin — as Kauśika did concerning the rivers?

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ācakṣva bhagavann etad yathā vidyām ahaṃ tathā balākāndhābhisaṃbaddhaṃ nadīnāṃ kauśikasya ca
english: Arjuna said: Tell me this, O blessed one, that I may understand it — the tale bound up with Balāka and the blind one, and the tale of the rivers and of Kauśika.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca mṛgavyādho 'bhavat kaś cid balāko nāma bhārata yātrārthaṃ putradārasya mṛgān hanti na kāmataḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa said: There was once a certain hunter of deer named Balāka, O Bhārata, who slew beasts to sustain his wife and children, not out of wanton desire.

sanskrit: so 'ndhau ca mātāpitarau bibharty anyāṃś ca saṃśritān svadharmanirato nityaṃ satyavāg anasūyakaḥ
english: He supported his blind mother and father, and others who depended on him; ever devoted to his own duty, truthful in speech, and free from malice.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin mṛgāṃl lipsur nānvavindat prayatnavān athāpaśyat sa pītodaṃ śvāpadaṃ ghrāṇacakṣuṣam
english: Once, eager for game and striving hard, he found no quarry; then he caught sight of a beast of prey that had drunk water and saw by scent alone.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvam api tat sattvaṃ tena hataṃ tadā anv eva ca tato vyomnaḥ puṣpavarṣam avāpatat
english: That creature, the like of which he had never seen before, he then slew; and at once a rain of flowers fell down upon him from the sky.

sanskrit: apsarogītavāditrair nāditaṃ ca manoramam vimānam āgamat svargān mṛgavyādhaninīṣayā
english: And a delightful celestial chariot, resounding with the song and music of Apsarases, descended from heaven to bear that hunter of deer away.

sanskrit: tad bhūtaṃ sarvabhūtānām abhāvāya kilārjuna tapas taptvā varaṃ prāptaṃ kṛtam andhaṃ svayaṃbhuvā
english: For that creature, O Arjuna, had by its austerities won a boon for the destruction of all beings, and had been made blind by the Self-Existent.

sanskrit: tad dhatvā sarvabhūtānām abhāvakṛtaniścayam tato balākaḥ svaragād evaṃ dharmaḥ sudurvidaḥ
english: By slaying that beast, which was bent upon the annihilation of all beings, Balāka thus went to heaven. So hard to know is dharma.

sanskrit: kauśiko 'py abhavad vipras tapasvī na bahuśrutaḥ nadīnāṃ saṃgame grāmād adūre sa kilāvasat
english: There was also a brāhmaṇa named Kauśika, an ascetic but of little learning, who is said to have dwelt at the meeting of rivers, not far from a village.

sanskrit: satyaṃ mayā sadā vācyam iti tasyābhavad vratam satyavādīti vikhyātaḥ sa tadāsīd dhanaṃjaya
english: "I must always speak the truth" — this was the vow he had taken; and so he became renowned as a teller of truth, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: atha dasyubhayāt ke cit tadā tad vanam āviśan dasyavo 'pi gatāḥ krūrā vyamārganta prayatnataḥ
english: Now once, in fear of robbers, certain people entered that forest; and the cruel robbers too came on, searching diligently for them.

sanskrit: atha kauśikam abhyetya prāhus taṃ satyavādinam katamena pathā yātā bhagavan bahavo janāḥ satyena pṛṣṭaḥ prabrūhi yadi tān vettha śaṃsa naḥ
english: Then, coming up to Kauśika the truth-teller, they said: "By which path, O reverend one, did those many folk go? Adjured by your truth, speak; if you know where they are, tell us."

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭaḥ kauśikaḥ satyaṃ vacanaṃ tān uvāca ha bahuvṛkṣalatāgulmam etad vanam upāśritāḥ tatas te tān samāsādya krūrā jaghnur iti śrutiḥ
english: Thus questioned, Kauśika spoke to them a truthful word: "They have taken shelter in this forest, thick with trees and creepers and thickets." And so, the tradition tells, those cruel men found them and slew them.

sanskrit: tenādharmeṇa mahatā vāgduruktena kauśikaḥ gataḥ sukaṣṭaṃ narakaṃ sūkṣmadharmeṣv akovidaḥ aprabhūtaśruto mūḍho dharmāṇām avibhāgavit
english: By that great unrighteousness, that ill-spoken word, Kauśika went to a most grievous hell — unskilled in the subtleties of dharma, of scanty learning, a fool who knew not the distinctions of duty.

sanskrit: vṛddhān apṛṣṭvā saṃdehaṃ mahac chvabhram ito 'rhati tatra te lakṣaṇoddeśaḥ kaś cid eva bhaviṣyati
english: He who, without asking the elders to resolve his doubt, deserves thereby to fall into a great pit. In this there will be some mark and indication for guidance.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ paramajñānaṃ tarkeṇātra vyavasyati śrutir dharma iti hy eke vadanti bahavo janāḥ
english: The highest knowledge is hard to attain; herein one determines it by reasoning. "Sacred revelation is dharma" — so say many people.

sanskrit: na tv etat pratisūyāmi na hi sarvaṃ vidhīyate prabhavārthāya bhūtānāṃ dharmapravacanaṃ kṛtam
english: Yet this I do not gainsay; for not all is ordained therein. The teaching of dharma was made for the welfare and thriving of living beings.
